info.name: MakeMyBrand API (App)
info.description:
App/frontend-facing endpoints of the mmb-api (admin endpoints excluded). Base path `/api/{{api_version}}`.

**Getting started**
1. Select the *MakeMyBrand App (Local)* environment.
2. Run **Auth → Send OTP** then **Verify OTP** (dev/staging returns the OTP; the scripts auto-save tokens).

Tokens and created resource ids are captured into environment variables automatically.

**Conventions**
- Every response is the envelope `{ success, data, meta? }`.
- Catalogue filters accept a **slug** (preferred), a uid, or a legacy numeric id; `*_id` params are deprecated.
- `industry` is the public name for a business category.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Mobile OTP login for users; email+password for admins.

Run **Send OTP → Verify OTP** to populate `access_token`. Run **Admin Login** to populate `admin_access_token`.

request.description: purpose: `login` | `reset`. In development/staging the response `data.otp` is returned and auto-saved to the `otp` env var.

exec: if (d.otp) { pm.environment.set('otp', d.otp); console.log('Saved otp', d.otp); }

request.description: Authenticates the user and auto-saves `access_token` + `refresh_token`. The collection default auth is `Bearer {{access_token}}`, so every user request inherits it.

item.name: Users
item.description: Signed-in user profile, settings, sessions and GST/billing details.

request.description: Carries `has_password` (whether the OTP-only account has set one yet) and the `onboarding` block (`account_type`, what step is still open).

Allow-list of writable fields — everything else on the user is server-owned.

`account_type` (`business` | `personal`) answers signup step 2 and can only be set while onboarding is still open (409 afterwards); `personal` completes onboarding immediately.
`profile_photo_s3_key` must be a key issued to you by `POST /uploads/presign` with slot `profile_photo` — `null` clears it.
For accounts with `has_password: false`. No current password is required — the live session is itself the product of an OTP. 409 if one is already set (use PATCH). Ends all OTHER sessions.
Returns 409 when `current_password` does not match.
Always a full object — defaults are applied for users who never saved any.

Partial update — send only what changed. `languages` is "Preferred Languages": a multi-select of **content** languages deciding which templates the user is shown, NOT the app UI language. It is a full replace (`[]` resets to the default) and entries are codes/uids/ids from `GET /languages`; an unknown one is a 400 naming it.

The `notify_*` flags cover TRANSACTIONAL messages only — OTP delivery ignores them.
Ends every session but this one. Effective immediately — each revoked session's access token is blacklisted, not just its refresh token.
Switches the account off and ends EVERY session including this one — discard the tokens after calling. Nothing is deleted; an admin can reactivate.
One billing record per user — creates or updates in place. `gstin` must be exactly 15 chars (or null/empty).

item.name: Businesses
item.description: Owner-scoped business management, the Brand Kit (keywords, palette, fonts, watermark), the public "Near Me" storefront, and adopted (premium) variants.

request.description:
`industry` is the public name for the business category and accepts a **slug**, uid, or numeric id. `category_id` is the deprecated legacy form (still accepted).

`sub_industry` is the child pick under `industry` (list them with **Catalog → Sub-Industries**); `custom_sub_industry` is the "Others" path — free text typed when the owner's trade is not in that list. It files a PENDING industry for admin approval and links the business to it right away (the chip stays hidden publicly until approved). The two are mutually exclusive — sending both is a 400.

The "Others" body is the sample below plus:

```json
{ "industry": "{{industry_slug}}", "custom_sub_industry": "{{custom_sub_industry}}" }
```

`industry` is **required** alongside it — a suggestion with no parent has no context for the admin reviewing it (400). A name that already exists converges on that row instead of filing a duplicate (case-insensitive), and a name an admin previously rejected is refused.

`keywords` must already exist in the tag catalogue — see `GET /industries/{ref}/keywords` for the suggestions; an unknown keyword is a 400 naming it.

`logo_s3_key` / `cover_s3_key` must be keys **you** were issued by `POST /uploads/presign` for slots `business_logo` / `business_cover`; a key from another namespace or slot is rejected.

`heading_font_id` / `body_font_id` come from `GET /fonts` (a premium library font needs a paid plan). `watermark_enabled: 1` needs the `custom_watermark` plan feature (403 otherwise) — turning it off is always allowed.

One business per account: a second create is a **409**, so once you are signed up the industry pick (including "Others") moves to **Set Sub-Industry / Others** below.

Every create field is patchable, `industry` / `sub_industry` / `custom_sub_industry` included (see **Set Sub-Industry / Others** for that trio). `watermark_enabled: 1` is plan-gated (`custom_watermark`) and 403s on a free plan; `heading_font_id` / `body_font_id` need ids from `GET /fonts`.

The **"Others" industry** flow — the owner cannot find their trade in `GET /industries?parent={{industry_slug}}` and types it instead.

What happens: the text is filed as a **pending** child of `industry` (`status: pending`, `is_active: 0`), the business is linked to it immediately, and the label stays hidden from the public catalogue and storefront until an admin approves it in **Admin → Business Categories** (`?status=pending`). Your own `GET /businesses/{uid}` shows it right away with `BusinessCategory.status: "pending"`, which is what renders the "pending approval" chip.

Rules worth knowing:
- `industry` is **required** with it — no parent, no review context, 400.
- `custom_sub_industry` and `sub_industry` are mutually exclusive; sending both is a 400.
- 2–100 characters.
- Names are globally unique and case-insensitive, so re-sending an existing name joins that row rather than filing a duplicate — an already-approved name simply becomes a normal pick.
- A name an admin has **rejected** is refused with a 400.

Picking an existing child instead? Swap the key for `sub_industry` (slug, uid or numeric id of a child of `industry`).

At signup the same two fields go on `POST /businesses` — see **Create Business**.
Soft delete, owner only.
The "My Keywords" card — the tags describing the owner's products & services.

Full replace — send the complete list, not a delta; `[]` clears it. Entries are numeric ids, slugs or display names that must already exist in the tag catalogue (there is no custom-keyword path). An unrecognised entry is a 400 naming it, never a silent drop.
Ordered array of `{ hex, label? }` — always an array, `[]` when unset.

Full replace; `[]` clears it. **Order is the meaning** — the first colour is the primary and is preserved exactly as sent. Max 6. `hex` must be the full 6-digit form (`#1A2B3C`; 3-digit shorthand is rejected) and is stored upper-cased, so `#ff0000` and `#FF0000` are one colour. Repeating a colour is a 400.
Active businesses within `radius` km of lat/lng, with a computed `distance_km`.
Public-safe storefront fields only (contact, hours, rating, geo, category).
Variants added to this business, each with its active template cards.

The button says brand series, but the grant is per-VARIANT — adopting one does not unlock its siblings. Requires the owner's ACTIVE plan to entitle the variant (403 otherwise). Idempotent, and the grant is durable — access survives a lapsed plan.

item.name: Projects
item.description: User designs (canvas documents) and their export records.

request.description: All of `business_id`, `template_id` and `size_id` are optional, and all three are **numeric ids**, not uids — unlike the rest of the app API, which addresses things by uid. Nothing in this collection captures a numeric business id, so they are left out of the sample body; fill them from `GET /businesses`, `GET /templates` and `GET /template-sizes` when you need a project bound to a template.
status: `draft` | `published` | `archived`.
export_type: `download` | `share`; platform: `whatsapp` | `instagram` | `facebook` | `direct`.

item.name: Products
item.description: Products/services of a business (shown on the public storefront).

request.description: `business_uid` is required.

item.name: Frames
item.description:
The frames store. Frames are admin-authored catalogue content — categorised, and either free or bought outright for a per-frame price. Note a paid PLAN never unlocks one: what you own is exactly what is in My Frames, and it survives a lapsed subscription.

Browsing is public; owning needs a token. Run **List Frames** first to fill `{{frame_uid}}`.

query.description: Category slug, uid or legacy id. An unknown value returns an empty page, not the whole store.

request.description: Active frames only. The design payload (`content`) is never in a list response.
The store's filter chips, in display order.
`content` is served only once you own the frame — a free frame still has to be added first.
Free frames only — a premium one is refused with 403. This is also the re-add path for a frame you bought and later removed, which costs nothing the second time.

Creates a Razorpay order for the price plus GST and records the purchase as pending. Confirm it with **Subscriptions > Verify Payment** — frames reuse that endpoint rather than adding a second one — or let the webhook do it.
What you own. Pending purchases and removed frames are excluded.
Takes it off the shelf. A paid frame stays re-addable for free. No refund.

item.name: Uploads (my files)
item.description:
Direct-to-S3 uploads for the signed-in user. Same Design B as the admin side (presign straight to the FINAL key tagged `status=pending`, then a tag flip on confirm), with one difference that carries the whole security model: **every key is derived from the caller** and lives under `users/{your uid}/{slot}/`. The client never sends a key or a prefix, only a slot name — and every write that accepts an `s3_key` (logo, cover, product image, profile photo) re-checks the key was issued to you for that slot.

**Flow:** `POST /uploads/presign` → `PUT` the file to `upload_url` echoing every header in `required_headers` → `POST /uploads/confirm`.

**Bulk** is the same three calls: send `files: [...]` to presign (max 20) for all the URLs at once, `PUT` them in parallel (4–6 at a time), then confirm every key in one call. Confirm reports each key separately in `results` — a batch is **not** all-or-nothing, so one oversized file does not discard the rest, and a `200` does not mean every key made it. If *every* key fails the request itself fails (400/402), so single-file callers are unaffected.

Slots: `profile_photo`, `business_logo`, `business_cover`, `product_image`, `media_library` (the editor's "My Uploads"), `brand_font` (the only non-image slot). There is no frame slot — frames are catalogue content you add or buy, not something you upload.

Images are raster only (`image/jpeg|png|webp|gif`) — SVG is deliberately refused for user uploads. Fonts (`woff2`/`woff`/`ttf`/`otf`) are checked on extension as well as content type, since browsers report font MIME types inconsistently.

Size is enforced at **confirm** (10 MB) — a presigned PUT cannot carry a size condition — and an oversized object is deleted rather than promoted. Unconfirmed objects stay `pending` and are swept by the bucket lifecycle rule, so an abandoned upload costs nothing. Confirm is also where storage quota is charged (402 when the plan's limit is reached).

request.description: Returns `{ key, upload_url, required_headers, expires_in, max_bytes, storage_remaining }`. `filename` is used only for its extension — the stored name is a uuid.

Up to **20** files in one call; slots may be mixed. Returns `{ files: [{ key, upload_url, required_headers }], expires_in, max_bytes, storage_remaining }` — the limits are per ACCOUNT, so they are reported once instead of on every entry.

Unlike confirm, presign IS all-or-nothing: the whole batch is validated before any URL is issued, so one bad entry 400s the request with a `files.3.filename`-style field path. Nothing has been uploaded at that point, so there is nothing to unwind.

`storage_remaining` is the headroom for the whole account, not per file — sum the batch client-side against it before uploading. The cap matches confirm's, so anything presigned together can be confirmed together.

exec: const d = (pm.response.json() || {}).data || {}; const f = d.files || []; if (f[0]) pm.environment.set('my_upload_key', f[0].key); if (f[1]) pm.environment.set('my_upload_key_2', f[1].key);

request.description: The font slot for a user's own Brand Kit typeface. Register the confirmed keys with `POST /fonts`.

Promotes pending → active, up to 20 keys per call. Rejects any key outside your namespace and any key with no object behind it.

Outcomes come back **per key** in `results` (`confirmed` | `rejected`, with a `reason` and `code`), and `keys` lists the confirmed ones only — so it is always safe to save straight onto records. Read `results`: files that pass are promoted and charged even when others in the same call fail. Only when EVERY key fails does the request itself fail, with the first error (400, or 402 when storage ran out).
One call for the whole batch. Inspect `results` for the per-key outcome — a `200` here can still contain rejected files, and `keys` holds only the ones that were actually promoted.
Same promotion, but records the dimensions and the user's own filename the media grid needs — the server cannot work those out without decoding the file. Send `uploads` **or** `keys`, never both.

The same figures presign returns, without having to start an upload: `{ limit_bytes, used_bytes, remaining_bytes, unlimited, max_upload_bytes }`. Read it when sizing a bulk upload, or to render a "82 MB of 100 MB used" bar.

Everything is in **bytes**, so it compares directly against a file size. `GET /subscriptions/me` reports the same allowance in MB for the plan's feature list — do not mix the two units.

`limit_bytes` / `remaining_bytes` are `null` when the allowance is unlimited or unenforced (a free account); check `unlimited` rather than testing for null. `used_bytes` is always real, so consumption can be shown either way. `max_upload_bytes` is the per-FILE cap, separate from the allowance.

Newest first. Defaults to the `media_library` slot — logos, covers and product images are managed on their own screens, so nobody can delete their logo from a media grid by accident. Prepend `cdn_base_url` to `s3_key`.

exec: const d = (pm.response.json() || {}).data; const first = Array.isArray(d) ? d[0] : null; if (first && first.uid) pm.environment.set('my_upload_uid', first.uid);

request.description: Removes the file and refunds its bytes against the plan quota. **Warn the user first** — a saved design that used the image will render it broken, and nothing links a project to the uploads it uses (project content is an opaque blob).

item.name: Fonts
item.description: Brand Kit typography — the curated library plus the user's own uploads, in one list. Assign a font to a business with `heading_font_id` / `body_font_id` on `PATCH /businesses/{uid}`.

request.description:
Optional auth — send `Bearer {{access_token}}` to include your own uploads and unlock premium library fonts. `is_own` marks yours; `is_locked` marks a premium library font your plan does not include (it still appears, but its files are withheld).

Each row carries its `FontFiles` (weight, style, format, s3_key) and `Languages` (script coverage). `?language=ta` narrows to fonts that can render that script — fonts with no declared coverage are always included, since unclassified means unknown, not incapable.

Turns files uploaded to the `brand_font` slot into a selectable family. Upload each file first (`/uploads/presign` → `/uploads/confirm`), then send the keys here — a key you did not upload to that slot is a 400.

Ship **both** `ttf`/`otf` and `woff2` where you can: the Flutter app cannot render woff2, and the web editor wants it. 409 if you already have a family with this name.
Removes the family and its files and refunds the storage. A business using it falls back to the default typeface rather than breaking. Library fonts cannot be deleted (403).

item.name: Feedback
item.description: In-app feedback. Signed-in users only, so every submission is attributable and support has someone to reply to. Admins read it under **Admin → Feedback**.

request.description: `rating` is the five faces on the Feedback screen, 1 (worst) to 5 (best), and is required; the note is optional. Rate limited — a burst returns 429.

item.name: Templates (public)
item.description:
Optional auth — send `access_token` to unlock premium content and raise the rate-limit tier, or none for anonymous.

The browse view **must be anchored**: at least one of `category` or `industry` is required (400 otherwise). All taxonomy filters accept a friendly slug, a uid, or a legacy numeric id.

Variant templates are NOT browsable here — they are premium and plan-gated, served only via `GET /variants/{uid}`.

exec: const d = (pm.response.json() || {}).data; const first = Array.isArray(d) ? d[0] : (d && d.items && d.items[0]);

request.description: Premium templates return `is_locked=true` with `content` withheld unless the caller is a paid user.

item.name: Assets (public)
item.description: `category` (the anchor) is required. Premium assets return `is_locked=true` and omit `s3_key` for guests/free users.

item.name: Catalog (public)
item.description:
Public read-only reference data — no auth required (a token only raises the rate-limit tier and targets audience-specific content).

Taxonomy filters (`parent`, `group`, `category`) accept a **slug**, a uid, or a legacy numeric id. The `*_id` forms are deprecated aliases.

request.description:
The public "industry" catalogue (business categories). Use `parent=null` for top-level industries, `tree=1` for the whole forest nested parent→child, `hierarchy=1` for the top level only, and `q=` to substring-match a name (`q` applies to the flat and `parent`-filtered shapes; `tree`/`hierarchy` ignore it). `with_related=1` attaches each row's curated SEO cross-link block (`RelatedIndustries`).

Only APPROVED, active rows are listed here, so a sub-industry a user filed through `custom_sub_industry` is absent until an admin approves it.

Step 2 of the signup industry picker: the children of the industry chosen in step 1. `parent` takes a slug, uid or numeric id.

These are exactly the values `sub_industry` accepts on `POST /businesses`. When nothing here fits — including the common case of an empty array, since most seeded industries have no children yet — that is the **"Others"** path: the app shows a free-text box and sends `custom_sub_industry` instead (Businesses → **Set Sub-Industry / Others**).
One industry by slug, uid or legacy numeric id, always carrying `RelatedIndustries` — the curated, editor-ordered cross-link block (active industries only).

The curated keywords for one industry. A sub-industry ALSO inherits its parent's keywords — merged and de-duped, its own first — so a bakery's picker offers the bakery keywords ahead of the generic food ones. `ref` is a slug, uid or numeric id. These are exactly the values `POST /businesses` and `PUT /businesses/{uid}/keywords` accept.
Deprecated backward-compatible alias of `GET /industries`. New clients should call `/industries`.
Set `tree=1` for the full active hierarchy nested parent→child (each node carries a recursive `children` array, ordered by display_order). `parent`/`parent_id` are ignored in tree mode.

Active content languages in display order. These select which TEMPLATES a user is shown — they are **not** the app's UI language. Render `native_name` ("தமிழ்"), which is what a speaker scans for; `name` is the English label for admin screens. Save the user's picks with `PATCH /users/me/preferences`.

Active brand series with their style personalities, tags and colour palette, the counts the card renders (`variants_count`, `templates_count`), and a preview slice of variants. `is_locked` is a ROLLUP of the variants — gating lives on the variant, so a series reads as locked only when every variant is.

exec: const d = (pm.response.json() || {}).data; const first = Array.isArray(d) ? d[0] : null;

request.description: Filter by brand series — `series` accepts a slug, uid or numeric id. The pre-rename `group` / `group_id` params are still accepted.

exec: const d = (pm.response.json() || {}).data; const first = Array.isArray(d) ? d[0] : null;

item.name: Get Variant (templates always listed, locked ones stripped)

request.description: The variant card is public, and so is the TEMPLATE LIST — templates are always returned so a visitor can see what they would be buying. When the caller is not entitled, `is_locked=true` and every template comes back WITHOUT its `content` (thumbnails only). Send `Bearer {{access_token}}` to be entitled — guests are always locked. Opening a template or starting a project from one is still refused while locked.
Active FAQ categories with their FAQs nested.
`category` narrows to a single group and accepts a slug, uid, or numeric id (`null` = the uncategorized group).
Active, in-window app banners — audience-targeted by the caller's tier.

Active events falling in a date window, each with `occurs_on` and its active `Templates`. Recurring events match on month-day, one-offs on `full_date`. Default window is a rolling week; use `range=month` or explicit `from`/`to`. The window is echoed in `meta.range`.
Active plans with billing options, card-visible features, `trial_days`, and applicable coupons. Use `plan_type=access_pass` to fetch the one-time ₹10 pass.

item.name: Config
item.description: Public app settings (`is_public` app-settings rows, typed).

item.name: Subscriptions
item.description: Plan purchase (Razorpay one-time + recurring), coupons, trials, the ₹10 access pass, and the current entitlement state.

request.description: The ACTIVE subscription with its plan, billing cycle, and per-feature entitlements (limit/used/remaining, or `enabled` for booleans). Poll after checkout to detect activation. `has_active_subscription: false` ⇒ treat as free tier.
Applies the full redemption rule set (validity window, `max_uses` cap, plan restriction, audience). 404 = unknown/expired; 409 = exists but not redeemable.

Creates a pending subscription and returns a Razorpay order (one-time) or a subscription `short_url` (recurring). A bad coupon fails the request rather than silently charging full price; `used_count` is consumed only on activation.

exec: const oid = d.razorpay_order_id || (d.order && d.order.id); if (oid) pm.environment.set('razorpay_order_id', oid);

request.description: One-time pass, allowed once per user ever (409 afterwards). Grants the access-pass plan's features for `pass_days`, then reverts to free.

exec: const oid = d.razorpay_order_id || (d.order && d.order.id); if (oid) pm.environment.set('razorpay_order_id', oid);

request.description: Post-Checkout UX confirmation; activates idempotently. The webhook remains the source of truth.
Deprecated alias of the public `GET /plans`. New clients should call `/plans`.
